plugin_desc: IT Watchdogs WeatherGoose climate SNMP child template for devices under IT Watchdogs PEN 17373. Interface traffic is supplied by the shared NetworkService SNMP IF-MIB floor rather than a plugin-side ifHC expansion. Proven wxGoos private increments under 1.3.6.1.4.1.17373.2 are climateTempC as env_temperature_celsius and climateHumidity as env_humidity_percent, with climateName as the sensor tag. Rows with climateAvail 0 are dropped. CPU, memory, fan and PSU scalars are not invented. V3/V4 trees and airflow/light/sound relative gauges are not collected in this pass. Supported brands/models - IT Watchdogs WeatherGoose climate monitors that expose the wxGoos climateTable and standard IF-MIB.
name: NetworkService

metrics.name: env_temperature_celsius
metrics.description: Per-sensor environment temperature in degrees Celsius from wxGoos climateTempC (1.3.6.1.4.1.17373.2.2.1.5). The SNMP value is already Celsius. Rows with climateAvail 0 are dropped. Empty climate tables yield no rows. Persistently high values may indicate cooling or ambient-temperature risk.

metrics.name: env_humidity_percent
metrics.description: Per-sensor relative humidity in percent from wxGoos climateHumidity (1.3.6.1.4.1.17373.2.2.1.6). The SNMP value is already 0-100 percent. Rows with climateAvail 0 are dropped. Empty climate tables yield no rows.

metrics.name: interface_ifHCInOctets
metrics.description: This metric indicates the average rate of inbound bytes received over the past 5 minutes, based on the 64-bit ifHCInOctets counter which does not wrap on high-speed interfaces.

metrics.name: interface_ifHCOutOctets
metrics.description: This metric indicates the average rate of outbound bytes sent over the past 5 minutes, based on the 64-bit ifHCOutOctets counter which does not wrap on high-speed interfaces.

metrics.name: snmp_uptime
metrics.description: This metric indicates the uptime of the device since the last restart. By monitoring the uptime, network administrators can understand the stability and reliability of the device and identify potential reboot or failure issues.
